name: Thatcherism
summary: The political and economic approach of Margaret Thatcher's governments (1979-90): sound money and monetarism, tax cuts, privatisation, curbs on trade unions, wider home and share ownership, and a rolled-back state in the economy but a strong state in law, order and defence. It pairs free-market economics with traditional morals, national sovereignty and Euroscepticism.
scope: The Thatcher-era program, drawn from the 1979 Conservative manifesto, Thatcher's Bruges speech and Wikipedia accounts of her policies and Gamble's 'free economy and the strong state' summary. Later Conservative leaders and post-Thatcher neoliberalism are excluded; the pre-1979 manifesto was cautious on privatisation and unions, which later grew into flagship policies.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The NHS was declared 'safe in our hands' and the manifesto promised no cut in its spending, though it also encouraged private provision.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Free markets, financial discipline and the claim that central planning does not work are the core of the doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: Privatisation of state industries and opposition to further nationalisation are flagship positions.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The manifesto pledged to cut income tax at all levels and cut the top rate to the European average, rejecting the politics of envy.

unions-good.rationale: The manifesto accepts that responsible free unions could help recovery but blames union privilege for the winter of discontent and legislated to curb union power.

property-fundamental.rationale: A property-owning democracy and opposition to wealth tax and nationalisation show strong support for property rights, though not as an absolute bar to government action.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Deregulation (the 1986 Big Bang, less intervention in industry) was the direction, though competition policy bodies were kept under review.

cut-welfare.rationale: Thatcherism targeted abuse and a 'dependency culture' and concentrated help on those in real need, but did not dismantle the welfare state.

worker-ownership.rationale: Employee share-ownership was encouraged, but collective ownership of firms by workers is the socialist model it rejected.

strong-leader.rationale: Power was centralised in the prime minister and conviction politics bypassed colleagues, though the manifesto upholds parliamentary supremacy.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is to be rolled back in the economy but kept strong in law, defence and order ('the free economy and the strong state').

empower-police-military.rationale: The manifesto promised more spending on crime-fighting even while economising elsewhere, full implementation of police pay recommendations and significant defence increases.

decide-locally.rationale: Local government was constrained through rate-capping and the poll tax, and devolution was opposed.

rehabilitation.rationale: The manifesto favoured tough sentences and a 'short, sharp shock' regime, while allowing community sentences for lesser offences.

traditional-family.rationale: Thatcherism is described as family-centred and promoted Victorian bourgeois virtues; support for family life was one of the five tasks.

abortion-legal.rationale: Thatcher voted for the 1967 abortion bill, but the movement was not committed on the issue and treated it as conscience.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christianity was invoked as a moral basis for enterprise and personal responsibility, but no program for a larger public religious role.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Bruges speech stressed keeping national heritage and identity intact; Lawson tied free markets to British nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Thatcherism respected Parliament and moved gradually on unions, but openly overturned the postwar consensus.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The 1979 manifesto calls firm immigration control essential and promises to limit family entry, severely restrict work permits and bring all entry for settlement under a quota system.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about other international bodies (such as the EU, WTO, IMF or WHO) or about support, funding or reform without enforcement powers, and the statement now asks whether the UN should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.

reviewHistory.rationale: The Bruges speech opposed supranational power; cooperation is via NATO and alliances of states.

free-trade.rationale: The manifesto rejected import controls as a socialist panacea, while keeping safeguards against dumping.

nation-first.rationale: Thatcher fought for a British budget rebate and defended national interests against Brussels.

open-borders.rationale: Firm border control is explicit policy; open borders contradict it.

limit-growth.rationale: Restoring growth and incentives is the aim of the program.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Thatcher backed climate science bodies and a treaty in 1989 but later shifted; the movement holds no settled line.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The manifesto sought a 'proper contribution from nuclear power' alongside coal.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): the old wording asked whether revolution is sometimes justified, and this disagreement rested on a preference for reform or lawful means, which doesn't say revolution is never justified.

reviewHistory.rationale: Rule of law and parliamentary supremacy are core commitments.

central-planning.rationale: The Bruges speech asserts that central planning and detailed control do not work.

socialized-markets.rationale: Public ownership was rejected even with markets; private ownership was the goal of privatisation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The manifesto attacked the damaging features of capital transfer tax and rejected a wealth tax.

basic-income.rationale: Policy stressed work incentives and reinforcing job-acceptance rules; an unconditional income conflicts with this.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Import controls were rejected, though temporary help and anti-dumping measures were accepted.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Government plans and subsidies cannot produce revival; the National Enterprise Board was to be curtailed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: A property-owning democracy via council house sales, share ownership and small business.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Money and sound money, wages and incentives are central; the idea is socialist-communist.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Controlling money supply through publicly stated targets is central to monetarist policy.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Pay bargaining was to be left to companies and workers, and corporatist social contracts were blamed for the crisis.

one-party-rule.rationale: Parliamentary democracy and the rule of law are core commitments.

democracy-best.rationale: The manifesto stresses parliamentary democracy and the supremacy of Parliament.

direct-votes.rationale: The party insisted on Parliament at the centre; referendums only to be discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: Parliament must stand at the centre of national life, not outside bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: Union of Britain maintained, Scottish devolution opposed.

political-violence-never.rationale: Violence and intimidation by pickets and terrorists was not tolerated; no amnesty for terrorists.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Thatcher said Christianity is about spiritual redemption, not social reform.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rule of law, police and defence are core state tasks in the strong-state doctrine.

military-superiority.rationale: The manifesto said significant increases in defence spending were needed to meet Soviet superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Rights of all citizens are equal whatever race, colour or creed.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The manifesto rejected the politics of envy and urged cooperation between classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Incentives, rewards for success and attacks on the politics of envy.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Bruges speech opposed forced unity of identity, though it endorsed the Atlantic community.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Self-reliance is praised, but the manifesto frames it as helping people to help themselves and others.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The manifesto stresses balance of rights and duties, while Thatcherism is individualist.

restore-past-order.rationale: Victorian values and traditional morality sit with a dynamic market agenda; the two strands split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Thatcherism was avowedly ideological conviction politics, though it adjusted pace by what was feasible.

direct-action.rationale: Violent and intimidating picketing was condemned; change was to come via Parliament.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The program stresses that hard work pays and success is rewarded.

production-for-use.rationale: Profits are the foundation of a free enterprise economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profits are the foundation of a free enterprise economy and the common interest of workers and management.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A Marxist doctrine opposed to parliamentary democracy and the rule of law. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

collective-farming.rationale: Private property, farming enterprise and small ownership are supported. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Marxist thesis was opposed; the free enterprise world was the free world defended against communism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxes were to be cut sharply, but the state's core functions were funded by them.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individualism and equal rights before the law; group rights not part of the program.

positive-liberty.rationale: The doctrine stressed freedom from state interference and a dependency culture.

organic-representation.rationale: Parliament, not outside groups, should be the centre of political decisions.

total-state.rationale: The state's role should shrink in the economy and over individuals.

national-rebirth.rationale: The manifesto spoke of a country that has lost its way and a new beginning, but not of radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Defence of Britain and allies, not expansion; the Falklands was a recovery of territory.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Parliamentary democracy and the rule of law are core. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

bound-labor.rationale: Free labour markets and free economy. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

universal-morality.rationale: Christian and Victorian moral standards were treated as binding, though not framed as reasoned universals.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The manifesto backed the Israel-Egypt peace; no direct statement on the principle.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The government restricted rights of abode by new nationality law.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The manifesto said it would be wrong to impose participation systems by law.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: A gradual reduction in the borrowing requirement was vital to controlling inflation.

economic-freedom.rationale: Thatcher drew on Hayek's argument that intervention leads to authoritarianism. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

rule-by-example.rationale: Law, police and strong sentencing were central to order.

national-self-determination.rationale: Britain defended Falklands self-determination and Rhodesia's democratic wishes.

force-without-un.rationale: Britain went to war in the Falklands and allowed US bases for the Libya raid.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Christianity was invoked as a basis for values.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Rules about the unemployed accepting available jobs were to be reinforced.

class-collaboration.rationale: The manifesto said government, unions and employers have a common interest and should be on the same side.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The manifesto proposed a National Heritage Fund and support for the arts.

ban-interest.rationale: Sound money and credit markets are central; deregulated finance. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The manifesto affirmed equal rights before the law whatever race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist thesis; the state is a neutral protector of law. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The program promoted North Sea oil production and a competitive coal industry.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The manifesto valued minorities' contributions and urged language training, with no demand for cultural assimilation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state kept welfare, the NHS and education roles.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equality before the law whatever race. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The rights of all citizens are equal before the law whatever race, colour or creed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal treatment before the law whatever creed.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rhodesia settlement was to rest on the democratic wishes of its people.

population-transfer.rationale: The manifesto said there could be no compulsory repatriation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Force is accepted for law enforcement and defence; the doctrine does not treat all initiation of force as wrong.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Competition and incentives drive growth in the program; the claim about peoples is not endorsed.

separated-powers.rationale: A strong second chamber and a Parliament controlling the executive were defended.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine opposed to parliamentary politics. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Help was to be concentrated on those in real need, but laws should reward effort and not rank groups.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The manifesto promised council tenants a legal right to buy their homes with discounts of up to 50 per cent.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The manifesto's immediate changes limited picketing, required secret ballots for closed shops and made unions bear strike costs.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Thatcherism ended the prices and incomes policy and relied on markets; price controls ran against its monetarist, free-market core.

party-controls-media.rationale: Free-market, anti-statist and committed to a free press, despite disputes with the BBC.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armed forces serve the Crown and state under parliament; the manifesto stressed defence through the constitutional state.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Bruges speech opposed a European superstate and defended the nation-state against supranational power.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Thatcherism upheld parliamentary sovereignty and the Westminster cabinet model over executive command.

church-by-bishops.rationale: She defended the Church of England's establishment but clashed with its bishops, so no clear view on governance.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Her program stressed national defence and loyalty, and she would not back an enemy's victory over Britain.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Thatcher treated NATO as essential to defence and the manifesto raised defence spending.

people-in-arms.rationale: The manifesto prioritised strong professional armed forces and the police; an armed citizenry is not part of the program.

death-penalty.rationale: Thatcher personally supported restoring capital punishment for terrorist murders.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The traditional-morals strand supported restricting obscene material.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The 1979 manifesto promised a new nationality law and the 1981 Act ended automatic citizenship by birth.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not a theme; the government conceded some Welsh-language provision but favoured a common national culture.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetarism aimed at stable prices, but the Treasury kept control of policy; the Bank was not made independent until 1997.

collective-defense.rationale: Thatcher treated NATO as the basis of defence and strongly supported the alliance.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The strong-state formula rested on law and order, with government under the rule of law and Parliament.

land-redistribution.rationale: Thatcherism defended private property and widened ownership through sales rather than seizure, so it rejects expropriating estates.

common-currency.rationale: Thatcher opposed a single European currency and monetary union as a loss of national sovereignty.

no-bailouts.rationale: Her governments refused to subsidise 'lame ducks' and championed market discipline, though some rescues occurred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: She defended parliamentary sovereignty and the rule of law but also distrusted rights adjudication by courts; adherents split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Thatcherism was committed to free trade and open markets.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: She opposed the EU Social Chapter and regulation imposed through supranational agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: Thatcherism relied on material incentives, tax cuts and enterprise as the spur to work.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Thatcherism held that free-market capitalism is robust and self-correcting if the state keeps money sound and markets free.

delink-world-market.rationale: It championed free markets and open trade and capital flows, and the government dismantled exchange controls.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: It combined economic liberty with a strong state in law and order; adherents are not libertarian on discrimination, though they opposed heavy regulation.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The manifesto stresses the supremacy of Parliament and the Bruges speech opposed supranational power over it.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Rights of all citizens are equal whatever race, colour or creed, and she did not rank by ancestry.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The program favoured open markets and inward investment, though strategic and defence exceptions existed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property and owner-occupation (right to buy) were central to the property-owning democracy.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty was central, including the Bruges speech defence of national parliaments.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Its focus on the family and tax cuts did not include explicit pronatalist policy, and it accepted immigration under controls.

job-guarantee.rationale: Thatcherism held that jobs come from the private market and rejected state employment schemes and nationalised industry.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: It stressed a strong state in law and order and the duty to uphold the law.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: It paired free-market economics with traditional morals and the family.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Bruges speech defended national sovereignty against supranational power and Thatcherism was Eurosceptic.

religious-nation.rationale: It stressed Christian morality and the Church of England, but defined the nation by citizenship, not faith.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: The program stressed private property, home ownership and share ownership and opposed common ownership of industry.

defeat-communism.rationale: Thatcher was a Cold War hawk, backing NATO and a firm line against the Soviet Union, though she also engaged Gorbachev.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The 1979 program encouraged private provision alongside the NHS and later reforms brought in internal markets.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Thatcherism held that free-market capitalism creates the wealth and freedom on which society depends.

socialized-care.rationale: The program stressed the family and individual responsibility and rejected expanding the state into domestic life.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Thatcherism favoured individual enterprise and private property and opposed collective ownership.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Thatcherism held the free-market economy to be the sound basis for society and rejected any middle way between capitalism and socialism as a road back to collectivism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Thatcher's governments kept the 1967 decriminalisation and never proposed re-criminalising, though Section 28 (1988) restricted its promotion by local authorities.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The program paired a strong state in law and order with parliamentary democracy and the rule of law, and sought to curb union power by statute rather than banning opposition.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Thatcherism favoured representative parliamentary government and attacked union and local-authority militancy; it promoted individual choice, such as share and home ownership, rather than collective participation.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Thatcherism defined itself against collectivism and consensus politics, rejecting the idea of a middle way between left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Thatcherism defended capitalism and wage labour as the basis of prosperity and choice, and rejected Marxist critiques of work under capitalism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Thatcher drew on Christian moral language, but the program grounds government in parliamentary consent and law; adherents' views on divine authority are not set out.

social-market-economy.rationale: Thatcherism accepted a safety net and competition rules but rejected the German-style social market and corporatist consensus as too statist; Keith Joseph still used social-market language in 1975, so the lean against is contested.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The 1979 manifesto made strengthening national defence a priority, and Thatcher's Bruges speech defended NATO and a strong British defence.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Thatcher was a committed Atlanticist and Cold War hawk who backed NATO and hosted US missiles; the Bruges speech stresses NATO as the guarantor of defence.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1979 programme and Thatcher's government accepted the universal franchise; its appeal to property owners was through home and share ownership, not restricting the vote.

reification.rationale: This is a Marxist analysis of capitalism; Thatcherism held that markets are the expression of individual choice, not a force dominating people.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: It defended private ownership and the market as guarantors of freedom, rejecting the claim that wealth makes press freedom hollow.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Thatcher governments rested on equal citizenship in the British state; a racial franchise is incompatible with that, although her immigration rhetoric was restrictive.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The 1979 manifesto promised a strong state with more police and tougher law enforcement.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential-risk policy was not a Thatcherite topic; she did raise climate change in 1989 but nothing defines a stance.

rent-control.rationale: Thatcherism sought to free the housing market, and rent controls were seen as damaging private renting.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The program stressed individual responsibility and a strong state, but state-run drilled youth movements are not part of it.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The government hosted US cruise missiles and Thatcher defended nuclear deterrence, so opposing nuclear weapons on UK territory is against it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Thatcher strongly backed the Atlantic alliance and US bases in Britain.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Thatcherism defended property ownership and wealth creation as legitimate rewards.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Thatcherism treated politics as pragmatic and economic; its moral language was Christian but not apocalyptic.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Water, buses and other local services were privatised or deregulated, although the NHS was kept public.

municipal-property.rationale: Council house sales and privatisation aimed at private and individual ownership, not municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Her governments curbed local councils and abolished the Greater London Council, favouring central authority over local confederation.

family-wage.rationale: Thatcherism stressed traditional family but opposed wage floors, so adherents are split on a family wage.

person-over-state.rationale: Thatcher stressed individual responsibility and the individual over the collective, famously saying there was no such thing as society.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty was central to her politics, as in the Bruges speech, and she resisted devolution.

capital-controls.rationale: Her government abolished exchange controls in 1979 as part of its free-market programme, and opposed state direction of capital.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Thatcherism stressed strong defence and national resolve, as in the 1979 manifesto's defence commitments and the Falklands War, so refusing to fight is rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The 1979 programme set out to curb union power and later governments favoured individual and enterprise-level bargaining over national collective deals.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Sound money and control of public borrowing were central, through the Medium Term Financial Strategy; these were policy targets rather than binding legal rules, so it stays at +1.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Thatcherism sought to roll back the state's economic role while defending constitutional institutions and the rule of law, not to destroy the state.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Her governments kept and upgraded the deterrent (Trident) and hosted cruise missiles, and she opposed unilateral disarmament.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The 1980, 1982 and 1988 Employment Acts curbed the closed shop, so adherents back freedom not to join a union.

women-suffrage.rationale: Thatcher herself held the highest office; conservatism of the period took equal political rights for women as settled.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Thatcherism was defined by opposition to socialism and state planning and by Cold War hostility to the Soviet bloc.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The government held that the Falkland Islanders' wishes were paramount in the dispute with Argentina, though the principle was not applied generally.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The 1979 programme stresses law and order through police, courts and sentencing, never killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Thatcherism was Atlanticist, anchoring defence and foreign policy in NATO and the US alliance rather than courting China.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about general consumption tax levels, and the statement now asks only whether basic necessities should be exempt.

reviewHistory.rationale: The 1979 budget cut income tax and roughly doubled VAT, shifting the burden to spending, so adherents would not cut consumption taxes.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about general consumption tax levels, and the statement now asks only whether basic necessities should be exempt.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Thatcherite welfare reform favoured selectivity and aid to those in real need over universal provision.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The rhetoric of ending support for 'lame ducks' and of competition opposes special favours to business, though privatisation was criticised for favouring insiders.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Thatcherism paired enterprise and modernisation with 'Victorian values' and traditional morality.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Thatcherism favoured rewarding effort and ownership and opposed levelling outcomes, treating inequality from enterprise as just.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: It scrapped exchange controls and liberalised finance, so a tax on currency trades runs against its free-capital stance.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Its free-market, anti-Marxist economics and union curbs rejected the labour theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: It joined national sovereignty and patriotism to a popular capitalism of home and share ownership aimed at working people.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Thatcherism was fiercely anti-communist and anti-socialist and backed market capitalism under elected government.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Thatcherism targeted abuse and a 'dependency culture' and concentrated help on those in real need, but did not dismantle the welfare state. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Council tenants should have a legal right to buy their homes.
missingStatements.rationale: The right to buy was a headline 1979 pledge, central to the aim of a property-owning democracy.

missingStatements.text: The law should restrict strikes and picketing, for example by requiring secret ballots.
missingStatements.rationale: Limiting picketing, closed shops and strike funding was among the three changes to be made at once in 1979.

notes: One Nation wing and later Thatcherites would answer some social questions differently. Wikipedia accounts of Thatcher's own views are used for several social and foreign-policy answers; many such answers are low confidence.
